newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson Breweries settles Coors dispute.
newsitem.headline: Molson Breweries settles Coors dispute.

text.p: Canadian brewer Molson Breweries said on Wednesday that it has settled a dispute with U.S. brewer Adolph Coors Co. in their battle over Molson's licensing rights to Coors' top-selling beers in Canada.
Under the agreement, Molson paid Coors C$100 million ($71 million) and will take a C$32.5 million ($23 million) after-tax charge against fiscal 1997 earnings, the company said in a statement.
Molson said it also agreed to form a new partnership with Coors and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd. to manage Coors brands in Canada.
Last October, an arbitration panel tore up Molson's contract for Coors Light and Original Coors, which accounted for 8 percent of the Canadian brewer's sales volume.
The panel said Molson breached its licensing deal by allowing Miller Brewing Co. to buy a 20 percent stake in the Canadian brewer in 1993 without Coors consent.
Molson Breweries continued to brew and sell Coors beers in Canada under an interim agreement until the dispute was settled. Miller Brewing is a unit of Philip Morris Cos. Inc.
Molson Breweries is also owned 40 percent each by Foster's Brewing Group and Toronto-based Molson Cos. Ltd.

"We are delighted to be able to put our legal issues behind us. We look upon this as a long-term relationship between parties that know and enjoy the beer business and who have shown in recent months that they can work well together to continue Coors Light's growth as the No. 1 light beer in Canada," Molson and Coors said in a joint statement.
Molson, Coors and Foster's have also entered into a conditional agreement to form a partnership to manage Coors brands in Canada.
The proposed partnership will be owned 50.1 percent by Coors and 24.95 percent each by Molson and Foster's.
